title: The Intercession of the Wise and the Fall of Solomon
english: It is an inheritance and an asylum, which time does not consume and a robber does not take away. For it is incorporeal and without body, trading among incorporeal souls.

You see how even the glorious and the un-songworthy Israelites, being deprived of all things and cast out from the land, were not deprived of or stripped of the title of being called from the God-loving forefather; but even while serving barbarians, they were freed because of the righteousness of the fathers, and while living in the desert, they were nourished because of the good reputation of those born; and though sinning continually and blaspheming many times, and being worthy of the destroying punishment, they were made worthy because of the merciful Abraham, and because of Israel they obtained forgiveness, impudent children being saved by the old age of the fathers.

And you know, O lover of learning, how at first when God called Moses from the shepherdship to the leadership of the peoples, He immediately says these things to the servant: 'I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:6). And having become a little person of the Word, He adds these: 'Gather the assembly of the sons of Israel and say to them: The Lord, the God of your fathers, appeared to me, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob' (Exodus 3:16).

And thus in preambles, God seals the descendants with the name of the righteous fathers, like a certain sign, knowing it to be good and profitable to be known from them. But after time had passed, when the people turned toward insolence against the Benefactor and despised the Savior, and they applied themselves to the idol-making of the calf and worshiped a lifeless skull, having lost the living and rational intellect,
Moses, not having such things as these to appease the Master on behalf of the disciples, the much-toiling pedagogue flees to the memory of the fathers and with them the entreaty...

It is cast, he says, in this way: having remembered Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the saved ones, before whom you swore to yourself that their seed would multiply like the stars of heaven (Genesis 22:17).

Great is the wrath and the fury, and it is unavoidable; but the wise and resourceful petitioner, having surrounded himself with the countenances of the saints and having cast down to God the cities of the elders through their memory, extinguished the punishment like a flame, healing the wounds with the paternal oil of those who remain.

Leaving the Mosaic book, he moved on to the books of the Kings. For there also he is seen worthy of pity, because he was the offspring of a God-loving father. And this is Solomon, the one of many thrones; who, since as time went on he was not a ruler of sufferings, but rather a slave and more uncontrolled in the flesh, and because of the heedlessness of life, he changed and subverted the ancestral piety, shaping idols that are stumbling blocks to the law.

God says to him: 'I will tear your kingdom apart and give it to your servant; however, in your days I will not do this because of David your father; from the hand of your son I will receive it' (1 Kings 12:9). These things instruct us through history; and the song of the Psalms teaches similar things: 'I was young; and indeed I have grown old, and I have not seen a righteous man left abandoned, nor his seed seeking bread' (Psalm 37:25).

But, as it seems, when once the soul of truth is shattered and it has rushed headlong into innovating instead of living in order, nothing is able to turn it back to the straight and ordered way; but resisting the bridle, just as a stubborn donkey is led toward the pit, overcoming the rider in mind by the impulse toward evil, such is it to see these Eunomians also.
For thus these men love to be called men rather than of Christ, blaspheming God and dishonoring the men of God, but rather...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Honor of Martyrs and Introduction to Euphemia
english: Whether they are being awed by the resting places of the saints, or are acting with prudence toward the altars and the defiled places. The ascetics of that deprivation and those who consider the terror against all things to be virtue thought that the shouts of the demons would be ashamed of the bright power of the martyrs crying out and shouting, and of those calling each one by name as if present, and driving away and chasing the oppressed humans.

Whether one wishes to say that the spirits of the athletes of piety act against the unclean spirits, or that angels attend the holy tombs in honor of those who have rested, it makes no difference; for whatever is said, it is the glory of those who suffered for the love toward Christ. The benefits of the martyrs appear manifest every day, sometimes in different and diverse ways, which free the wanderers from the operations of the satanic. For those who were once seized by madness and held by evils are now seen to be acting with prudence, and we see the boldness of the embassy of the saints testifying to the facts.

And just as unmistakable proofs of the power of our Savior were contained in the midst of the Hebrews—those cleansed of leprosy, those whose sight was healed, the blind, and if any paralytic, having been strengthened in the harmony of his limbs, walked without hindrance—so also now those who carry the cross for the sake of Him who was crucified provide clear proofs by the grace of the Lord, healing the faithful in various and diverse ways like fellow-slaves.

And Paul and Peter—the one having expelled the Python demon (Acts 16:18), the other having raised the lame man at the temple gates (Acts 3:6)—turned Hebrews and Greeks toward obedience to the gospel through practical powers; but the evil assembly of heretics now badly harasses our...

The martyrs are not respected even for the greatness of the miracles. Instead, people call them many-maned, and their tombs and their resting places are named as such, and they cleanse themselves as if rubbing against a contagion, not even mentioning that God-breathed saying praised by every mouth: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints' (Psalm 116:15). Therefore, let us pray to God, and let us call on the martyrs to implore our common Master, so that a spirit of compunction may be given to those acting under the error of heresy, and the division may be loosed like a dividing wall or a barrier, so that all may come together in brotherly unity in Christ Jesus our Lord, to whom belongs the glory forever. Amen.

The discourse of Asterius, Bishop of Amaseia, concerning the holy Euphemia the martyr. First, O men, I had Demosthenes in my hands, the formidable one, and those Demosthenian things where Aeschines strikes bitterly at the memories; having been stained by the word and having thickened the intellect, I was in need of relaxation and a walk, so that the suffering of my soul might be somewhat released. Having come out of the room and having conversed a little with acquaintances in the marketplace, from there I arrived at the temple of God to pray at leisure.

As I happened to do this and was walking one of the covered walkways, I saw a certain painting there and the sight seized me intensely: you would say it was a work of Euphranor or one of those ancients who, having taken up the art of painting, worked great lifelike panels with little effort. Come here, for if you wish for a leisure narrative now, I will describe the painting to you; for we do not have medicines from the children of the Muses that are any less inferior than those of the painters. A certain woman, a holy virgin, having consecrated her chastity to God, they call Euphemia; and when a tyrant was once driving away the pious, she eagerly sought death.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Artist's Depiction of the Passion
english: Danger; but the citizens and sharers in the religion for which she died, having marveled together at her courage and the sacredness of the virgin, having placed the shrine near the temple and laid down the casket, perform honors to her and make the annual feast a common and widespread celebration, a panegyris.

Therefore, the celebrants of the mysteries of God always honor the memory by word and by intention, and they teach the associated people with care how she completed the contest of endurance. And the painter himself, through his art, having engraved with all possible power the whole history upon linen, placed before the shrine a sacred spectacle; and here is the artistic skill.

A judge sits high upon a throne, looking bitterly and with hostility at the virgin; for he is angry whenever the art [seeks] even with soulless materials. And there are spear-bearers of the ruler and many soldiers; some carrying the tablets of the memoranda and styluses, one of whom, having raised his hand from the wax, looks intensely at the one being judged, turning his whole face, as if rising to intercede, speaking so that she might not write incorrectly or errantly concerning the hearing, being weary.

And the virgin stands in a purple tunic and robe, signifying philosophy, as it seemed to the writer, and her appearance is charming, as it seems to me, the soul having been beautified by virtues. And two soldiers lead her toward the ruler, one pulling her by the face, the other hurrying from behind. The appearance of the virgin is gripped by modesty and severity; for she indeed bows toward the earth as if reddening the faces of the men, but she stands unshakeable, suffering nothing in the cowardly contest.
If I had previously praised other painters, I would have beheld the drama of that woman of Colchis, as she is about to bring to the children the...

A sword divides the face with mercy and anger; one of the eyes manifests wrath, while the other manifests the mother being pitied and trembling. Now I have shifted the wonder of the Scripture from that idea to this one; and I am most ignorant of the artist, because he has rather mixed the bloom of colors, combining shame and courage together, through natural sufferings.

Moving forward into the face of the imitation, certain criminals in small tunics, already naked, were beginning the work; and the one, seizing the head and leaning it toward the back, provided for the other a suitable position for the punishment of the virgin's face; and the assistant was cutting out the pearly teeth; and a hammer and a chisel appear as the instruments of the punishment. My eyes weep from here, and the passion strikes my speech; for the painter has colored the drops of blood so vividly that you might say they are truly flowing from the lips, and you would depart mourning.

After these things, a prison; and again the solemn virgin sits alone in light-colored garments, stretching out her hands toward heaven and calling upon God, the helper of the distressed. While she prays, the sign appears above her head, which indeed the law commands Christians to worship and to inscribe, a symbol I think of the passion which was receiving her.

Immediately, indeed, and after a little while, the painter kindled a fierce fire elsewhere, making the flame by applying red color here and there. He stands her in the middle, having spread her hands toward heaven, showing no pain in her face, but on the contrary rejoicing because she has emigrated to the incorporeal and blessed life.

Up to this point the painter has set his hand and I too my speech; it is time for you, if you wish, to finish the Scripture, so that you may understand accurately, lest we have come much after the explanation.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
